name: Hinge Load & Broad Jump
focus: Loaded Posterior Chain to Horizontal Power
execution: Trap-Bar Romanian Deadlift (5 reps, 3s eccentric) + Immediate Broad Jump to Stick (1s)
swap: Single-Leg Dumbbell RDL (5/side, 3s eccentric) + Immediate Broad Jump to Stick (1s)

manual.why: Builds posterior-chain force and expresses it horizontally, the direction of a tennis first step, with a trap bar that can be dropped so the heavy-to-explosive pair has a safe exit.
manual.cue: Hinge back with a long spine, then let the bar go and jump - reach for ground, land soft and dead still for a beat.

goals: faster first step to wide balls

name: Face Pull & Prone Reach
execution: Cable Face Pull (12 reps, 2s hold at face) + Immediate Prone Y-Raise (8 reps, 2s hold)
swap: Band Face Pull at Anchor (12 reps, 2s hold) + Prone Y-Raise (8 reps, 2s hold)

manual.why: The serve is internal-rotation dominant and hammers the front of the shoulder; a face pull plus a prone reach rebalances it by training retraction and the low trapezius, the tissues that keep the shoulder centred through an overhead action.
manual.cue: Pull the rope apart to your face and hold it there, then reach thumbs up like you're holding a tray - the shoulder blade does the work, not the arm.

name: T-Spine Open & Overhead Reach
focus: Thoracic Extension to Overhead Serve Range
execution: Open-Book Thoracic Rotation (6/side, slow) + Immediate Banded Overhead Pull-Apart to Tall Reach (12)
swap: Open-Book Thoracic Rotation (6/side, slow) + Bodyweight Overhead Reach to Tall (12)

manual.why: A serve needs thoracic extension and a free overhead arm; if the mid-back cannot extend the shoulder pays for it, so this primes the range before a serving session rather than loading it.
manual.cue: Open the book slowly and breathe into the stretch, then reach tall and long - ribs down, don't arch from the lower back.

name: Calf Load & Pogo
execution: Dumbbell Single-Leg Calf Raise (8/side, 3s eccentric) + Immediate Two-Foot Pogo Hops (12, minimal contact)
swap: Bodyweight Single-Leg Calf Raise (8/side, 3s eccentric) + Two-Foot Pogo Hops (12, minimal contact)

manual.why: Tennis is thousands of push-offs a session, and the achilles and calf carry them; loading the calf through a slow eccentric then bouncing builds the tendon stiffness that absorbs that volume instead of breaking down.
manual.cue: Lower the heel slowly over three seconds, then bounce off the floor like it's hot - quiet feet, stiff ankle, no knee bend.
